recipes.name: Tender Pan-Fried Chicken Breasts
ingredients_raw: 8 (6 ounce) skinless, boneless chicken breast halves

steps.text: Line 2 baking trays with aluminum foil; set aside.

Stir together flour, salt, pepper, tarragon, ginger, mustard powder, thyme, garlic powder, and oregano in a shallow bowl until well-blended. Beat together egg and milk in a separate bowl until smooth.
Dredge chicken breasts in flour mixture, shake off excess, then dip in egg, and again in flour. Place coated chicken breasts on one of the prepared baking trays; set aside to rest for 10 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Dredge chicken breasts in flour once more; shake off excess.
Heat vegetable oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Cook chicken breasts in hot oil until golden brown, 2 to 3 minutes per side. Place fried chicken breasts on the second prepared baking tray.

Bake in the preheated oven until no longer pink in the center and the juices run clear, about 20 to 30 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read at least 165 degrees F (74 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Tender Pan-Fried Chicken Breasts
raw_recipe.description: This pan-fried chicken is coated in spices, pan-seared until golden brown, then baked until moist and tender for a delicious family weeknight dinner.

video.description: In this video, you’ll see how to make tender, moist chicken breasts that go from stovetop to oven. It’s a simple method that locks in the tasty juices. You’ll dredge the chicken breasts in a simple coating of flour, herbs, and seasonings, and then fry them quickly on the stove before finishing in the oven. So easy!

review.reviewBody: This is an excellent recipe for juicy, crispy chicken breast. I always read other reviews before trying any recipe and took the advise of another to put the chicken on a slotted baking pan to keep it from getting soggy. I didn't have any tarragon or ginger, but the crust was very well seasoned even without it. The mustard gave it a nice bite. However I did cut back on the pepper as suggested. I did find that the recommended amount of oil was not sufficient though. The flour soaked up a lot more than what was called for. You won't be sorry that you made this one.

I made this last night and I thought it was just okay-I did not like the fact that it became soggy on the bottom side after baking. However, my husband and mother in law really liked it! I did cut down on the salt and pepper-actually cut both in half. Next time I may try to bake the chicken breasts on some sort of rack-maybe they would not get soggy that way. I liked the idea of baking due to the fact that most often chicken breasts dry out when you fry them-and I don't like dark meat! I will try again with a few adjustments! Pretty good recipe.

Love this recipe. Used to buy frozen tenders, but I thought this recipe didn’t look too hard. After making it, I’ll never go back to flash frozen. Flavorful, juicy, my husband loves them, and he’s a fried chicken snob. We omitted ginger, tarragon, and mustard powder, but added in 1tsp rosemary, followed the other spices. I used the amount of oil that I thought was appropriate for my large pan. I used Bob’s Red Mill all purpose gluten free flour because I’m GF, it worked just fine. The 10 minute waiting time is critical for the breeding to stick. Since I use a whole pack of fresh breast tenders, it usually takes me about that long to get everything coated. I use a digital probe thermometer to make sure they’re done at the thickest part when coming out of the oven. We love them! They keep for a couple days in the fridge too for easy reheating. You won’t regret this!

I made some adjustments to the recipe because I made 6 thighs and 10 legs. I used a lot of flour (about 3-4 cups)which may have diluted the spices a bit though. I think about 2 teaspoons instead of a full tablespoon for each spice? I also decided to dip mine in breadcrumbs as well. First, dip in egg mixture, then flour, then back to egg mixture, then breadcrumbs. I used planko breadcrumbs for about 4-5 of them and the rest I used Italian breadcrumbs. My girlfriend and I loved them. I would suggest baking for a full 30-35 minutes like I did to get the most oil and grease out of them while keeping the tenderness.

Will make it again and again, it's the method I wanted, more than the seasoning mix (for my family taste buds). I had my own flour mix. 

Used egg/milk mix, and the two egg wash dips, and rested for 10 min. That's part of the key to tenderness. One last dusting of flour mix, fried, and baked on a cooling rack atop a cookie sheet covered with crumpled foil.

Very yummy, moist inside, crisp outside. Dipped in buttermilk then flour mixed with Panko bread crumbs and only used Seasoned Salt with California garlic sprinkle. Try using a butter and oil mix to fry in for the best flavor.

I just used the recipe for my family tonight and it was great. So did I do anything different, yes. I brined my chicken for a few hours, however, I do that all the time with my chicken. I used boneless, skinless chicken breasts. I cut the amount of salt, pepper and ginger in half. I didn't' have tarragon so I substituted basil in equal measure. After reading some reviews I added an extra cup of flour, I don't think I needed to but the spices didn't taste as if they overwhelmed the chicken. I then fried it in a cast iron skillet until brown and placed in oven for 15 minutes while I finished the sides. My family went crazy for this. I used some of the oil and some of the flour mixture to make gravy, it was outstanding. I will only use this one going forward.

This recipe was fantastic! The flavor was incredible! I cut the chicken up into nugget sized pieces and mixed up the spices a bit based on what I had available (add paprika!). I wish I'd read the review that advised to cook on slotted pan, because mine did turn out a bit soggy so I increased the temp to 400 and let them cool on a baking rack and it helped a lot. I will ?? make this again

Made this tonight to go with some fettuccini alla carbonara. We all loved it! The chicken was golden and crispy on the outside and juicy on the inside. Per some of the reviews I reduced the salt and pepper amounts by half, next time I will use the full amount. I recommend doubling the egg/milk mixture as I did not have enough. I also turned the chicken half way through the baking time to help make it crispy. We will be making this a part of our recipe rotation.

It was some of the tastiest fried chicken I've ever eaten! It was crispy, salty, juicy tender inside, fully cooked. I put it into my mouth and couldn't believe that I'd made it. It was THAT good.
The only changes I made were that I nixed the tarragon and added an extra sprinkle of garlic powder. I also used thighs instead of breasts. Baked them for 25 minutes exactly, perfectly cooked.
I took the skin off the thighs and lightly breaded them with some leftover breading and fried them separately while the chicken was in the oven. So. Tasty.

This was a fabulous recipe! I used chicken tenders instead of breasts. I didn't have Tarragon, but used all other spices listed. I did use 3 cups of flour to balance out the pepper. I used a broiler pan, flipped the chicken at 7 minutes and baked for an additional 9 on the other side. It turned out juicy, crispy and very tasty. The family absolutely loved this recipe! Thank you for sharing it
I used Panko bread crumbs for the final coating, gave the chicken some crunch!

I made this the other night and took the suggestions of cutting the salt down, and baking it on a wire to keep the crispiness. It definitely needed the salt that I took out, but otherwise it was a delicious meal
I've been using this recipe for several years. It's my go to for fried chicken. The breading really sticks to the chicken, it stays moist, and it tastes terrific! Highly recommend!
Very easy to make,, the breading fell off some places so need to figure that out.
I really enjoyed this recipe. I added some poultry seasoning.

This was easy to follow and had a nice flavor. It's a decent blend of herbs and spices and they all play well together. The chicken meat didn't have a lot of flavor itself though and needed something. I think this is okay, but it was missing something in the batter. Maybe more garlic, more pepper, onion powder, sage? Not sure, but it seemed like it needed something for depth. I did enjoy trying out this recipe. The chicken was perfectly done and not overcooked using this method and timing after just 20 minutes in the oven. The bottoms got wet from the juices running out from the meat as it cooked. It didn't affect the flavor, but the crust wasn't as crispy and crunchy as a result.
Didn't have the right spices to make this correctly so I supplemented. came out superb. Wife and kids enjoyed it.
Followed recipe exactly and it turned out delicious and moist! As suggested by others I did use a baking rack to avoid the soggy bottom problem. I'll definitely be making it again.
I should have known that this was not a recipe for us. There were simply too many ingredients. The chicken was tender, but the flavor lacked the wonderful crispiness and taste of southern fried.
